title: Prioritized cooperative cancellation for multiplexed streaming chat ergonomics
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a cooperative cancellation and prioritization layer in the Python SDK streaming stack to support multiplexed chat connections. Goals: let client code express per-conversation priority and cancellation semantics, ensure predictable backpressure without dropping high-priority user turns, enable graceful preemption and resumable partial outputs, and provide clear telemetry for preemption/cancel events.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a CancelToken/Handle usable by streaming consumer callbacks to request cooperative cancellation without losing already-emitted fragments
Support per-stream priority with a simple API (e.g., StreamPriority enum + attach to start_stream call)
Runtime honors priority during backpressure: when queue is full, lower-priority streams are soft-drained (slow/paused) before preempting higher-priority streams
Deterministic unit tests that simulate multiplexing, preemption, cancellation, and full replay using a test checkpoint serializer
Documentation + a small example notebook demonstrating priority escalation and graceful downgrade from streaming to non-streaming completion
Metrics emitted: preemptions.count, cancels.latency_ms, stream.queue_depth.p{50,95,99}, resumed.count
technical_notes: Design: add a cooperative cancel token that signals handlers; streams are responsible for checking token at stable boundaries (on fragment emit / on event handler entry)
Multiplexing: the connection-level multiplexer will keep a priority heap indexed by (priority, last_active_ts) to decide which streams to throttle under pressure
Checkpointing: introduce an abstract CheckpointSerializer interface (serialize_fragment, deserialize_fragment) so resumability tests can inject deterministic serializers for replay

Retry semantics: for preempted streams we will record last-stable-offset; retry will seek and resume using KV-cache-compatible resume token when backend supports it; for other models we will fall back to full non-streamed completion

Backpressure policy: configurable window (soft_window, hard_limit). Soft_window triggers pause/yield to lower-priority streams; hard_limit forces cooperative cancel and converts to non-streamed finalization path
Telemetry: attach tags (stream_id, priority, model, connection_id) to all preempt/cancel metrics and expose trace points for request lifecycle
API ergonomics: provide context manager and decorator helpers so existing user code requires minimal changes to adopt cancellation (e.g., with stream_session(priority=HIGH) as s:)
Security: cancellation metadata must not leak user PII; sanitize before emitting traces/logs
decisions: Use cooperative cancellation rather than forced socket aborts to avoid corrupt partial outputs and make client-side retries deterministic
Expose per-stream priority with three levels (LOW, NORMAL, HIGH); keep API surface minimal to avoid cognitive overload
Telemetry will be added to our existing metrics pipeline (prometheus & tracing); no new ingestion service
Default backpressure policy will be conservative: soft_window=80% of configured queue, hard_limit=120% (reject) with ability to tune via client config
